scenario: Exact-policy issuer for fresh guarded review writes with historical issuance recovery

stages.label: exact-policy-and-local-administrator
stages.explanation: A fresh retention plan is named by one exact rule for principal, actor and verdict. One separate administrator key creates the issuer. Duplicate rules, wrong administrator and four mismatching scopes fail before target reservation.

stages.label: admitted-native-guard-and-discarded-reply
stages.explanation: The complete successful managed-issue response is discarded. Own native show and status identify a fresh guarded job and separate holder key. Exact native prepare keeps its old owner path. Administrator and unrelated keys cannot step, a holder cannot issue, and a new request cannot adopt the existing job.

stages.label: issuer-revoked-holder-completes
stages.explanation: Administrator revocation blocks a new issuance before missing target reads. The native holder remains active and completes all three credential-required phases after that revocation. Exact issuer create and revoke retain historical responses; an issuer key does not revoke its child.

stages.label: historical-issuance-without-live-targets
stages.explanation: After native completion and issuer revocation, the actual complete discarded issue response is recovered exactly with the new plan, review and job offline. Changed requests conflict without live reads. Own receipt lookup also works while the issuer is offline; its historical receipt is unchanged.

stages.label: separate-holder-revocation
stages.explanation: After all paths return, the child is still completed and active despite issuer revocation. Its own holder then revokes native access, blocking new and cached protected steps. Exact managed issue, own receipt and exact native prepare remain historical and do not reactivate either authority.

stages.label: preserved-history-and-explicit-limits
stages.explanation: All four new paths return. Earlier six legacy write statuses, the completed revoked guarded job, released lease heads, blocked restore jobs and original lstat metadata remain unchanged. The new review is completed, its holder and issuer are separately revoked, and the immutable issuance remains historical.

limits: Exact issuance policy matches the public plan ID, principal, actor and verdict. Administrator and holder are self-declared labels and local bearer keys; external identity, semantic approval and domain authorization are not established.

The managed path creates a fresh native guarded job. Existing legacy or guarded jobs and incomplete receipts are never adopted or repaired. Native guarded prepare remains an independently supported owner path; native step still has issuer_policy_enforced=false and lease_enforced=false.

The issuer, issuance, job and review locks stay held until receipt synchronization under one cooperative deadline; plan capture briefly holds its own tail lock. This does not create an atomic transaction across directories.

A native Guard11 is durable before its separate managed issuance record. If receipt sealing fails, a fully valid active native guard and its already saved holder key may remain usable after unlock. An outer issue error therefore does not prove no capability or effect exists. This gap is documented, not injected in this normal scenario.

Issuer revocation blocks new managed issuance, preserving exact authenticated historical issue replay and old child guards. The holder completes three native phases after issuer revocation, then separately revokes its own guard. Neither revocation cancels already admitted effects or rewrites historical receipts.

The actual complete successful issue response is discarded and recovered exactly after child completion and issuer revocation with new plan, review and job offline. Own receipt lookup also works while the issuer is offline. Compact anchors do not reconstruct absent full native control bodies.

Four temporary new paths return in finally. Earlier private controls and public source/live histories remain unchanged. No archival, deletion, new restore, injected partial write, expiry wait or new fault worker is introduced.

Only public responses, credential markers and lstat metadata are read by this driver. Private controls, lease SQL and staging bodies are not read or exported. External LLM, semantic quality, process overlap, throughput and maximum agent capacity are not measured.
